atlas-nz.0065: Public Service graduate and internship roles are posted on NZ Government Jobs, and some programmes rotate graduates across agencies: the NZ Government Procurement programme placed 10 graduates in four six-month placements.
atlas-nz.0066: Summer of Tech helps New Zealand employers hire junior tech talent, with about 100 events a year for students and graduates; registration for its 2027 programme opens in January.
atlas-nz.0067: Tech graduates follow the national pattern of hiring people who have already worked for the employer: 63% of graduates had worked for their current employer before their graduate role.
atlas-nz.0068: The pages read set eligibility by study status, not school: Deloitte takes people finishing their studies or within 24 months of finishing, from all majors and degrees. Universities still host the expos and employer events through which firms meet students.
atlas-nz.0069: The University of Auckland’s 2026 expos were Business and Law on 12 March, Engineering and Technology on 21 and 22 April and Internship and Graduate on 29 July; no 2027 dates were listed. Summer of Tech opens its 2027 registration in January.
atlas-nz.0070: Graduate rounds cluster in the year before a February start, with different windows by employer: NZ Government Procurement 17 July to 17 August 2026, Suncorp New Zealand closing most streams on 31 August, Deloitte open by October for a 22 February 2027 start.
atlas-nz.0071: The programme pages read ask for a finished degree in any major, not a master’s: Deloitte takes people finishing their studies or within the previous 24 months. A level 8 or 9 qualification matters mostly for the post-study work visa, which now needs level 7 or higher.
atlas-nz.0072: NZQA evaluates overseas tertiary and vocational qualifications through an International Qualifications Assessment, and says to check with the organisation you apply to whether you need one; it advises applying only when you hold every required document.
atlas-nz.0073: The programme pages read name no target schools: Deloitte welcomes all university majors and degrees, so fit, results and work experience count more than the university name.
atlas-nz.0074: The graduate pages read show no dual-study route. Apprenticeship-type pathways exist beside them: Employment NZ lists Māori and Pasifika Trades Training and Skills for Industry pre-trades training as pathways to apprenticeships, but these lead to trades, not graduate roles.
atlas-nz.0075: Central government employed about 417,700 people, including education and health; the Public Service is a smaller part, with 42.6% of its workforce in the Wellington region. One graduate programme read there is the 10-graduate Procurement programme.
atlas-nz.0076: Some firms take international graduates who already hold work rights: Deloitte accepts a post-study work visa valid for three years. Employers that sponsor need accreditation and a job check; the post-study visa for level 7 and above lets you work for any employer, so you do not depend on a sponsor at first. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-nz.0077: No photo: Tahatū’s CV guide says not to use images.
atlas-nz.0078: Keep the CV to about 2 pages if you can, and tailor it to each job using keywords from the advert, which also helps with applicant tracking systems.
atlas-nz.0079: Deloitte’s application asks for a cover letter, a CV and an academic transcript.
atlas-nz.0080: If the advert asks for referees, list at least 2, one usually a current or former manager; if it does not, write “Referees available on request” and provide them if you are interviewed.
atlas-nz.0081: Deloitte asks for an academic transcript with the application; an NZQA International Qualifications Assessment for an overseas degree is requested only if the organisation needs it.
atlas-nz.0082: Graduate adverts show a band instead of asking for a figure: Baker Tilly Staples Rodway advertised NZ$50,000 to 60,000, and SEEK Grad showed NZ$50,000 to 80,000 for an entry-level service-centre adviser role at Victoria University.
atlas-nz.0083: Checks are common but bounded by law: an employer may contact only the referees you named, needs your written approval for a criminal record check from Police or the Ministry of Justice, and must follow the Privacy Act 2020.
atlas-nz.0084: Formal channels carry the programmes (employer websites, expos, LinkedIn) but word of mouth ranks beside them, and friends and family influence over two thirds of graduates.
atlas-nz.0085: A New Zealand degree is the clearest route: the post-study work visa is for up to 3 years, and from 16 November 2026 it extends to holders of a bachelor’s degree completed in New Zealand or overseas, plus level 7 graduate diplomas studied in New Zealand.
atlas-nz.0086: Check the work-rights line of each advert: Deloitte asks for evidence of the right to work and, for international students, a post-study work visa valid for three years.
atlas-nz.0087: English. The application stages read (cover letter, one-way video interview, face-to-face interview) run in English, and an accredited employer work visa for skill levels 3 to 5 requires proof of English.
atlas-nz.0088: Deloitte’s graduate selection has four steps: an application with cover letter, CV and academic transcript; a one-way video interview on HireVue; a face-to-face interview; then an offer by phone followed by a contract by email.
atlas-nz.0089: Poor communication is the number one reason interns withdraw from a process, and 41% of graduates received two or more offers, so speed and contact between steps matter.
atlas-nz.0090: Some employers run rotations rather than one role: the Procurement programme is four six-month placements over two years.
atlas-nz.0091: Every employee must have a written employment agreement, and employers should be open to negotiating terms if you ask; terms not written in do not remove the minimum rights set in law.
atlas-nz.0092: A trial period can last up to 90 calendar days for someone who has not worked for the employer before, but it must be agreed in the signed agreement before work starts and is not allowed for migrants on an accredited employer work visa. A probationary period is the alternative, with a fair process before dismissal.
atlas-nz.0093: Graduate adverts state a pay band, for example NZ$50,000 to 60,000 at Baker Tilly Staples Rodway, so there is little to negotiate beyond where in the band you start.
atlas-nz.0094: Check the work-rights line of each advert first: Deloitte accepts international students who hold a post-study work visa valid for three years and who show evidence of the right to work for the length of the role.
atlas-nz.0095: An employer that sponsors an accredited employer work visa must be accredited and hold a job check for the job; the job must be full-time at 30 hours a week or more, and you need 2 years of relevant experience or a qualification at level 4 or higher, where a bachelor’s degree in any field counts.
atlas-nz.0096: A level 7 or higher degree studied in New Zealand lets you work for any employer for up to 3 years on the post-study visa, which removes the sponsorship question for a first job.
atlas-nz.0097: Portals and boards: NZ Government Jobs for the Public Service, SEEK Grad (GradConnection NZ), which listed 122 graduate and internship programmes the day it was read, Trade Me Jobs, LinkedIn, and Tahatū for advice and tools.
atlas-nz.0098: Employer pages carry the programmes and dates: Deloitte (applications through SmartRecruiters), Baker Tilly Staples Rodway and NZ Government Procurement; Summer of Tech serves junior tech roles.
atlas-nz.0099: University career services run expos, such as the University of Auckland’s Business and Law, Engineering and Technology, and Internship and Graduate expos, and the New Zealand Association of Graduate Employers publishes the surveys cited here.
atlas-nz.0100: Starting the internship search late: Tahatū advises starting 6 to 9 months ahead because some programmes only accept applications at certain times of the year.
atlas-nz.0101: Skipping the internship: 77% of employers filled some or all of their graduate roles with people who had worked for them before, and 63% of graduates had worked for their current employer first.
atlas-nz.0102: Applying when the round has closed: NZ Government Procurement closed on 17 August 2026 for a February 2027 start, and Suncorp New Zealand closed most streams on 31 August.
atlas-nz.0103: Sending a CV with a photo or running past about 2 pages: Tahatū says not to use images and to keep to 2 pages if you can.
atlas-nz.0104: Counting on a trial period or visa sponsor: a 90-day trial is not allowed for migrants on an accredited employer work visa, and Deloitte asks international students for a post-study visa valid for three years.
atlas-nz.0105: Deloitte’s graduate stages (cover letter, one-way video interview, face-to-face interview) run in English; the pages read state no formal language test.
atlas-nz.0106: NZ Government Jobs and the Procurement programme page are in English; the pages read name no language test.
atlas-nz.0107: Summer of Tech works in English; for a work visa, an accredited employer work visa asks for proof of English for skill levels 3 to 5.
atlas-nz.0108: Retention is strong: median retention is 91% of graduates who started in 2024 still employed, and graduates intend to stay up to 3 years on average; 35% plan to work overseas before the end of 2027.
atlas-nz.0109: The wider market is soft: the unemployment rate was 5.6% in the June 2026 quarter, and the underutilisation rate of 15 to 24-year-olds rose from 33.6% to 37.0% over the year.
